title: Officials paid by, or invested in, the companies their departments pay

beats.text: Every year, San Francisco officials file a Form 700. It lists their outside income and investments.

visual.text: Outside income and investments, filed every year, so the public can see when a decision-maker has money riding on a decision.

beats.text: We matched those forms, and nonprofit tax returns, against what each official’s department pays.

visual.label: Matching
visual.sub: each form, against what the official’s own department paid

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. Disclosure is what the law requires.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The rule: an official must stay out of decisions that affect that source of money.

beats.text: Take a Public Works manager.
On his form: an investment in a builder, Charles Pankow Builders.
Worth over 1,000,000 dollars.
And what did Public Works pay that builder, in the years around his filings?
70.9 million dollars.

visual.label: paid by Public Works to Charles Pankow Builders Ltd

beats.text: A stake that big in a current contractor is the textbook conflict.
Yet he took the post in June 2025, and 51.9 million was paid before that.
